newsitem.title: USA: Italy's STET Group invests in Silicon Valley.
newsitem.headline: Italy's STET Group invests in Silicon Valley.

text.p: STET Group, owner of Italy's biggest telephone company, has invested $35 million in Silicon Valley companies in the past year, and is looking to invest more.

The parent company of Telecom Italia is tapping Silicon Valley's expertise in creating Internet content and entertainment so that it can increase the number of hours Italians spend browsing online, STET executives said Monday.

"Our main goal is to increase traffic through our network," said Martino Ajmone Marsan, president of Steam USA, the San Francisco-based venture capital arm of STET. "We are in active negotiation with lots of companies."

So far, STET has bought minority stakes in Concentric Network Corp., a San Jose, Calif., Internet service provider geared toward businesses; and Protozoa Inc., a San Francisco 3-D animation studio and software company.

Other than software and networking, STET also is looking to invest in companies that are developing devices other than personal computers to connect to the Internet, executives said. PCs are still relatively rare in Italian households.
STET has not set a specific budget for its venture capital operation, but could spend significantly more if it finds the right opportunities, said Umberto de Julio, STET's director general.

In the past decade, STET -- with 1996 revenue of about $25 billion -- has spent millions upgrading its telecommunication network to be among the best in Europe. The company can offer customers plenty of "bandwidth," or capacity to carry information, but no content.

De Julio said Italy has yet to develop a local version of California's Silicon Valley, which is why STET is investing here. STET hopes that by importing the technology, it can goad native start-up companies to create Italian entertainment and news services for the Internet.
